answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a unique, nontransferable stake in a vault, then require that stake to back actions that earn trust. A trellis of peer attestations raises the stake required for an agent whose history is thin, while losses from proven fraud are shared across identities funded from the same source. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to lock scarce capital per identity and risk losing it; an ember of reputation cannot simply be copied into a swarm.
